notes:
Top-level: fintech payments orchestration; latency-critical customer UX (two-step auth + realtime insights)

Summary: evaluation POC focused on achieving stable p99 latency under 120ms at peak throughput (~2k req/s) while hitting strict cost targets. Team is exploring Dedicated for production but needs a short Private/VPC POC for compliance. Very interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations: batching profiles, prefix/KV caching strategies, and quantization tradeoffs.

Timeline / recent activity:
- 2025-01-15: Intro call (Jordan + Priya) — CTO (Marta Varela) emphasized: "can't tolerate transient p99 > 200ms; customer drop-off is immediate".
- 2025-01-22: Tech deep-dive (SE: Priya) — collected model sizes, sequence length histograms, and current infra (k8s + managed GPUs).
- 2025-01-28: Sent baseline perf data (internal load test CSV) and requested Redwood perf-run.
- 2025-02-03: Fireflies meeting ff_20250203_6b9c — discussed canary/fallback routing and KV cache reuse for session affinity.
- 2025-02-10: Onsite bench run scheduled (remote) — Redwood to provide perf harness and kernel-level latency breakdowns.
- 2025-02-12: Security questionnaire submitted; waiting on SOC2 artifacts and data-residency confirmation.

POC scope and technical notes:
- Workloads: conversational agent (short-turn chat, avg tokens/request 40), real-time reranking (top-K=20), dense embeddings for search (128-d).
- Latency SLOs: p50 ~ 30-60ms, p95 < 80ms, p99 < 120ms under steady state 2k req/s. Cold-start budgets ok for dev, not for prod.
- Throughput: steady 1500-2000 req/s, spiky bursts to 5k req/s for Black Friday bursts.
- Cost target: keep inference unit cost under $0.0007 per token equivalent; prefer Dedicated pricing with autoscale/burst policy.
- Performance levers requested: continuous batching (max batch 128), dynamic batching thresholds, prefix/KV caching for returning sessions, quantization to 4-bit for 13B models, int8 for 7B models. Want Redwood Optimize to recommend batch sizes vs latency tradeoffs given their seq length distribution.
- Benchmarking asks: need per-kernel breakdown, memory vs latency tradeoffs, and sustained throughput graphs across 1m+ token runs. Also want side-by-side: fp16 vs int8 vs 4-bit quant profiles.
- Routing: require fallbacks to smaller model variant on capacity shortage; also zone-aware routing (primary us-east, fallback eu-west).

Security / compliance notes:
- Must run within customer's VPC for prod; strict egress controls, KMS for keys, and 7-year audit logs for certain financial models. Data residency: primary in US, some EU records must remain in eu-west region.
- Internal security flagged SSO/SAML, ISO/SOC2 proofs (SEC-4120).

Customer sentiment / quotes:
- Marta Varela (CTO): "We will spin up a prod flow only if p99 is predictable and auditors sign off."
- Head of Platform: "Batching is the secret — but we need smart defaults; don't want to tune for each endpoint."

Next steps (short):
- Redwood to run perf harness (w/ Priya) week of 2025-02-17 — focus: p99 + steady 2k req/s run + quantized 4-bit profiles.
- Security to deliver SOC2 artifacts by 2025-02-20.
- Draft Dedicated pricing and burst policy; propose canary rollout plan (A/B) and fallback model mapping.

Open blockers (short): network egress policy sign-off (infra), capacity footprint for private GPUs (ops), procurement window (legal).

Notes style: CRM shorthand — fragments, timestamps, links to drive and Fireflies above. Follow-up owner: Jordan Reyes.
